simple.meaning: מְעִיל (mᵉʻîyl) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a robe (i.e. upper and outer garment).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 28 times across Exodus, Leviticus, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, and 5 more, beginning at Exodus 28:4. Its contexts include family, family line, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְעִיל (H4598).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מְעִיל (mᵉʻîyl) / H4598 is traced through Exodus 28:4, Exodus 28:31, Exodus 28:34, Exodus 29:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a robe (i.e. upper and outer garment)

occurrences.englishText: These are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and his sons, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
“You shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.
You shall take the garments, and put on Aaron the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, and clothe him with the skillfully woven band of the ephod.
He made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.
The opening of the robe in the middle of it was like the opening of a coat of mail, with a binding around its opening, that it should not be torn.
They made on the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, scarlet, and twined linen.
They made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates around the skirts of the robe, between the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, around the skirts of the robe, to minister in, as Yahweh commanded Moses.
He put the tunic on him, tied the sash on him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the ephod on him and fastened it to him with it.
Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
As Samuel turned around to go away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him, and gave it to David, and his clothing, even including his sword, his bow, and his sash.
Afterward, David’s heart struck him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
May Yahweh judge between me and you, and may Yahweh avenge me of you; but my hand will not be on you.
May Yahweh judge between me and you, and may Yahweh avenge me of you; but my hand will not be on you.
He said to her, “What does he look like?”
She had a garment of various colors on her; for the king’s daughters who were virgins dressed in such robes. Then his servant brought her out and bolted the door after her.
David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who bore the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the choir master with the singers; and David had an ephod of linen on him.
When I heard this thing, I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled the hair out of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded.
At the evening offering I arose up from my humiliation, even with my garment and my robe torn; and I fell on my knees, and spread out my hands to Yahweh my God;
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me.
Let my adversaries be clothed with dishonor.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate,
I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh!

Then all the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones, and lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling. They will sit on the ground, and will tremble every moment, and be astonished at you.
